svg.title: Buffer size versus line availability for LATHE-01 to GRIND-01 with config MTBF/MTTR and with long repairs
svg.text: Buffer size vs. availability of a 2-station line – LATHE-01 → buffer B_CS1 → GRIND-01 (config MTBF / MTTR)
Planning approximation: A(B) = min over i of 1 / (1 + r_i + r_j · e^(−T_B / MTTR_j)), r = MTTR / MTBF, T_B = (B/2) · t_c (buffer half full on average), t_c = 190 s (grinder pace).
Config values: LATHE MTBF 30 h / MTTR 15 min, GRIND 40 h / 18 min
buffer places B between the two stations
Long repairs: same MTBF, MTTR 60 min each (typical when a spare is missing)
buffer places B between the two stations
• A buffer of B places hides a stop of the other station only if the stop is shorter than T_B = (B/2)·t_c. With B = 8: T_B = 4 × 190 s = 12.7 min.
• Repairs are exponential: the share of stops longer than T_B is e^(−T_B/MTTR). Config MTTR 18 min → e^(−12.7/18) = 0.49 of grinder stops still pass.
• To hide 90 % of the stops: T_B = −MTTR · ln 0.1 = 2.3 · MTTR → B = 2 · 2.3 · MTTR / t_c = 26 places for MTTR 18 min, 87 places for 60 min.
• Whole line of 16 stations in series without buffers: A = 1 / (1 + Σ r) = 1 / 1.077 = 92.85 %. Buffers + spare speed recover most of the 7 %.
• The buffer must also refill: the feeding station needs spare speed (here lathe 170 s < grinder 190 s). Verify with the twin What-if tab.
